title: After his Pittsburgh exit, what's next for Aaron Rodgers?
summary: As Aaron Rodgers enters waivers, the first question is whether any team will claim the balance of his one-year contract.
content: As Aaron Rodgers enters waivers, the first question is whether any team will claim the balance of his one-year contract. Obviously, no one will do it without ensuring that Rodgers actually wants to play for that team. Unless, of course, a team or two hopes to troll Rodgers by forcing him to show up to play where he doesn't want to play. Like Marty Schottenheimer did to Deion Sanders in 2002. So, yes, it would be hilarious if the Jets decide to put in the proper paperwork. The more likely outcome is that he'll clear waivers and become a free agent. It will give him the ability to sign with any team, at any time. No clear-cut contender currently needs a starter. And it would make no sense for Rodgers to sidle up to a quarterback-needy also-ran, like the Cardinals. Some have suggested that Rodgers could join the Patriots, who will be missing Drake Maye while they try to parlay 5-5 into playoff position. His August comments about the Mike Vrabel-Diana Russini situation would potentially be an impediment to that outcome. There's a spicy possibility of Rodgers aligning with the Ravens, who still play the Steelers twice. Is he that petty? At this point, it's impossible to say he's not. Rodgers's best play could be to wait. Let fate decide. Last year, Broncos quarterback Bo Nix broke his ankle late in a playoff win over the Bills. If Denver's instant desperation caused them to consider dusting off Drew Brees (despite the fact that he can't throw a football with his dominant arm), they would have surely called Rodgers, if he'd been available. Something like that can happen again. Of course, a team that loses its starter to injury between now and the Super Bowl would have to want to do business with him. Which means accepting the very strong possibility that, in time, Rodgers will have grievances to air about his experience. Because if it goes poorly, it won't be his fault. There will be other reasons for his struggles. Reasons that he has shown he has no qualms about sharing in his national-media safe space. During his 22-year career, Rodgers has played for three NFL teams. He ended up disgruntled in each location. If he adds a fourth franchise to the list, he'll likely find a way to be disgruntled there, too. Unless it's a very short-term arrangement. As short as one or two playoff games.

title: Christian Watson ruled out with a concussion
summary: Rams safety Kamren Kinchens was disqualified for the hit that injured Watson.
content: Packers wide receiver Christian Watson will not return for the second half of Wednesday night's game against the Rams. Watson went to the locker room for a concussion evaluation shortly before halftime and the Packers announced that he has been ruled out at the start of the second half. Watson had four catches for 65 yards and a touchdown prior to his injury. The Rams also lost safety Kamren Kinchens for the rest of the game on the same play. Kinchens was ejected for a helmet-to-helmet hit on Watson. Rams tight end Davis Allen has also been ruled out with an ankle injury. The two teams went to the break tied 13-13 and that remains the score early in the third quarter.

title: Chuck Clark, DJ Wonnum are inactive for the Lions
summary: The Lions will be missing a pair of defensive starters for Thursday's home game against the Bears.
content: The Lions will be missing a pair of defensive starters for Thursday's home game against the Bears. Safety Chuck Clark and defensive end DJ Wonnum are both inactive after being listed as questionable to play on the team's final injury report. Clark has a hamstring injury and Wonnum has a back injury. Clark's absence could lead to more playing time for Kerby Joseph, who will be playing his second game since being activated from the physically unable to perform list. The Lions will also be getting cornerback D.J. Reed back after he missed three games with a hip injury. Cornerback Ennis Rakestraw, defensive back Keith Abney, and defensive end Tyrus Wheat are also inactive for Detroit. The Bears have deactivated quarterback Case Keenum, cornerback Kyler Gordon, cornerback Isaac Yiadom, defensive back Elijah Hicks, running back Roschon Johnson, offensive lineman Jordan McFadden, and defensive lineman Jayden Loving.

title: Here's a roadmap to the Aaron Rodgers developments, one of the craziest stories in years
summary: If you were traveling on Wednesday or otherwise not plugged in for one of the most rollicking, unpredictable days in years if not ever, you're in luck.
content: If you were traveling on Wednesday or otherwise not plugged in for one of the most rollicking, unpredictable days in years if not ever, you're in luck. We've reconstructed the full timeline as to the events regarding now-former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers. It actually started on Monday, when coach Mike McCarthy was asked whether he has considered using one of the team's other three quarterbacks when the offense is struggling. McCarthy, whose body language in hindsight suggests he was dreading the question , said without equivocation, " Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback ." On Tuesday, Rodgers took his usual reps at practice. He conducted his usual midweek press conference. Unbeknownst to most of the media or the general public, the Steelers were changing their play-calling procedures to have quarterbacks coach Tom Arth, and not McCarthy, communicate the calls to Rodgers through the speaker in his helmet. Then came Tuesday night. At 11:10 p.m. ET, the Steelers issued a statement — not from coach Mike McCarthy or G.M. Omar Khan or owner Art Rooney II but from team spokesman Burt Lauten — that Mason Rudolph will start on Friday against the Broncos and Rodgers will be inactive. The news forced the Broncos to make a quick pivot in their preparations from Rodgers to Rudolph. As one source put it, the Broncos weren't sure whether it was a good thing or a bad thing . It was definitely a bad thing, all things considered, for the Steelers. By Wednesday morning, reports emerged that it was a coach’s decision . At 8:00 a.m. ET, McCarthy informed the team of the decision. Rodgers wasn’t there . As it turns out, he was excused . Enter Pat McAfee. He teased a surprise guest at 1:40 p.m. ET. As expected, it was Rodgers. Rodgers took a flamethrower to McCarthy, airing out dirty laundry that created a major mess for his now-former team. He exposed the fact that, at halftime of the Week 11 loss to the Eagles, McCarthy broke down the locker-room gathering by saying, " 1-2-3 Packers ." Rodgers also said McCarthy was falling asleep during some meetings and missing other meetings, expressing (in passive-aggressive fashion) concern for McCarthy's health. But Rodgers also said it was nothing new, and that McCarthy had done the same things in Green Bay, when they worked there together a decade ago. Rodgers also made it clear he wouldn't stay with the Steelers. After his session with McAfee and company, Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reported that the Steelers were expected to release Rodgers . By the official close of business, they’d waived him . A question lingers as to whether the Steelers will try to deny Rodgers the balance of his $22 million salary. It won't be easy; they'll need to both void the guarantees and wipe out his eligibility for termination pay (in the form of his remaining salary) under the Collective Bargaining Agreement. McCarthy met with reporters on Wednesday, after all hell had broken loose. He admitted to the "1-2-3 Packers" comment, calling it an " [e]mbarrassing moment ." McCarthy also said that Rodgers was benched after issuing an "ultimatum" that was " clearly outside of his job description ." ESPNFL thereafter reported that McCarthy " has the full support " of the organization, and that the team is "not planning to make any immediate changes." The key word may be "immediate"; with few viable options only two days before a Black Friday game against the Broncos, changes could come later. The overriding takeaway is that someone with the Steelers knew or should have known that McCarthy and Rodgers couldn't co-exist. Because, obviously, they didn't co-exist. If, as Rodgers claims, McCarthy believed Rodgers got him fired in Green Bay, McCarthy shouldn't have wanted a reunion with Rodgers. And if, as Rodgers claims, McCarthy was doing the same kinds of things in Green Bay that he did in Pittsburgh, Rodgers shouldn't have wanted a reunion with McCarthy. The reunion has now ended abruptly, with seven games left in the 2026 regular season. It remains to be seen whether Rodgers wants to play with another team, or whether another team wants him. Any team that signs him risks being on the receiving end of a future gripe session from Rodgers in which he lists all the things that team and/or the coach did wrong — without ever acknowledging his own role in the reality that it didn't work out. The good news, if there is any, is this: If Rodgers never plays again, his final NFL pass will have been a touchdown . Which is a better outcome than if he'd retired after the 2025 season. His final pass that year was a pick-six in the playoffs .

title: James Jones: I'm on text threads with former Packers, none are on Aaron Rodgers' side
summary: In the dispute between Steelers coach Mike McCarthy and ex-Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers, players who were with both of them in Green Bay are squarely on McCarthy's side.
content: In the dispute between Steelers coach Mike McCarthy and ex-Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers, players who were with both of them in Green Bay are squarely on McCarthy's side. That's the word from former Packers wide receiver James Jones, who echoed the comments of former Packers offensive lineman T.J. Lang , both of whom say that in text threads of former Packers players, everyone agrees that Rodgers' criticism of McCarthy was out of line. "How do you jump on Pat McAfee's show and say all this? Come on, man," Jones said on the Speakeasy podcast . "My text thread is full of texts and group chats with a lot of my teammates right now, and none are on 12's side, especially the ones that know Mike." Jones said that even if everything Rodgers said about McCarthy's shortcomings as a coach is true, airing dirty laundry in public is unacceptable. Jones said that when a coach and a player have the kind of personal history that McCarthy and Rodgers have, they should address their differences privately. "I don't even care if it's the truth," Jones said. "Have the conversation with Mike in there. This is not something you go to the media bashing somebody. I would not do this to people that I love." It's safe to say that there's no love anymore between Rodgers and McCarthy. But there is a lot of love for McCarthy among former Packers players, who are not happy that Rodgers chose to publicly attack their coach.

title: Jayden Daniels: Brandon Aiyuk and I put the past behind us
summary: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels and Brandon Aiyuk were once Arizona State teammates and close friends, but Aiyuk seemed to burn those bridges this year, when he posted several critical comments about Daniels on social media.
content: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels and Brandon Aiyuk were once Arizona State teammates and close friends, but Aiyuk seemed to burn those bridges this year, when he posted several critical comments about Daniels on social media. After Aiyuk signed with the Commanders this week, however, Daniels said that's all behind them. "I'm a grown man, he's a grown man," Daniels said. "Things happen. You don't know what he was going through. You don't know what I was going through at that time." Daniels said he looked up to Aiyuk when they were at Arizona State together and thinks they can have a good relationship as teammates again. "That's somebody that looked out for me when I was 18 years old, helped me out when I first got to ASU," Daniels said. "So, like I said, I know the character and the person he is. He was man enough to settle our differences and just move forward from there. That's like a brother to me. Like I said, we've been knowing each other for some time, looked out for me, took care of me. So, just put the past behind us." As for the social media posts that Aiyuk made, Daniels said he was never angry about that. "I prayed for him because he's like family to me," Daniels said. "I think that was a very dark moment in his life." Daniels declined to go into specifics about recent conversations with Aiyuk but said he hopes Aiyuk will be a good addition to the Commanders. "That's between us, personal, but yeah, we did chat," Daniels said. "He works hard. Before his knee injury he was All-Pro, very explosive, big catch radius, so excited for him to have a fresh start, new opportunity to prove himself day in and day out." Aiyuk hasn't played in more than two years, but he was once one of the best receivers in the NFL. If Aiyuk can play at anything close to the level he used to play at, he can be a significant addition to the Commanders' offense. Daniels is excited about that possibility.

title: Jordan Love, Christian Watson cut Rams lead to 13-10
summary: The points keep coming in the first half at SoFi Stadium.
content: The points keep coming in the first half at SoFi Stadium. A little more than three minutes after the Rams scored their first touchdown of the night, the Packers paid their first visit to the end zone. Jordan Love hooked up with Christian Watson for a six-yard score that cut the Rams' lead to 13-10 with just over eight minutes to play in the half. Watson also caught a pass on the first play of the drive and that completion went for 21 yards. Love hit Watson's fellow wideout Matthew Golden for a 39-yard gain on the next play and the quarterback scrambled for the third first down of the possession a couple of plays after that big gain. The Packers went three-and-out and turned the ball over on their first two possessions, but they are now outgaining the Rams thanks to back-to-back scoring drives.

title: Josh Jacobs inactive for Wednesday night's game, Micah Parsons officially active
summary: Packers running back Josh Jacobs returned to practice this week, but a return to game action will have to wait a little longer.
content: Packers running back Josh Jacobs returned to practice this week, but a return to game action will have to wait a little longer. Jacobs is inactive for Wednesday night's game against the Rams due to a finger injury. He was listed as questionable after being listed as a limited participant in all three practices this week. While Jacobs is out, defensive end Micah Parsons will be making his 2026 debut. Parsons was cleared for full action after last season's torn ACL and he was activated from the physically unable to perform list earlier this week. Linebacker Zaire Franklin, offensive lineman Jager Burton, offensive lineman Donovan Jennings, and offensive lineman Mekhi Becton are also inactive for the Packers. Quarterback Ty Simpson, defensive end Larrell Murchison, linebacker Darryl Peterson, center Coleman Shelton, guard Steve Avila, and linebacker Desjuan Johnson are the inactives for the Rams.

title: Kamren Kinchens: No ill intent on hit that concussed Christian Watson
summary: The Rams defense pitched a shutout in the second half on Wednesday night and they did it without safety Kamren Kinchens in the lineup.
content: The Rams defense pitched a shutout in the second half on Wednesday night and they did it without safety Kamren Kinchens in the lineup. Kinchens was ejected from the game just before halftime because of a hit to the head of Packers wide receiver Christian Watson. Kinchens was initially flagged for unnecessary roughness and the penalty was upgraded to a disqualification after video review by league officials. After the game, Kinchens said he couldn't really argue with the decision but that he didn't regret the play because Watson's injury was an unintended consequence of trying to make a play. "No ill intent ," Kinchens said. "I wasn’t trying to hurt the guy. Just playing football, fast physical football." Watson was ruled out for the rest of the game with a concussion and will have over a week to clear the protocol before the Packers' Week 13 game against the Saints.

title: Kyle Shanahan on Brandon Aiyuk signing with Commanders: "They got a good player"
summary: The Aaron Rodgers rigmarole has pushed plenty of other stories out of the spotlight.
content: The Aaron Rodgers rigmarole has pushed plenty of other stories out of the spotlight. Including the sudden second act for Brandon Aiyuk. Aiyuk visited the Commanders on Wednesday, two days after being released by the 49ers and one day after clearing waivers. He promptly signed with the team's practice squad. 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan was asked for his thoughts on Aiyuk landing with the Commanders. “None," Shanahan told reporters. "It was just a transactional thing and it's good for Washington. They got a good player.” Indeed they did. That's why the 49ers signed him to a four-year, $120 million contract only 27 months ago. They could have traded him to the Steelers. They paid him. It all fell apart after that, perhaps fueled by the lingering rancor of the protracted and contentious contract talks. Everyone hopefully learned a lesson. Now, the Commanders have a much-needed piece to the offense. A player who can help fill the void created when Terry McLaurin was lost for the season. And the Commanders — despite being 4-5-1 — remain in solid position to make a late-season run. With seven games to play, they're two games behind the Giants. The Commanders hold the tiebreaker, thanks to the 1-0-1 record in their 2026 head-to-head competition. The Commanders face the Cardinals, Titans, Texans, Falcons, Vikings, Jaguars, and Cowboys. The Giants have the Colts, 49ers, Seahawks, Browns, Lions, Cowboys, and Eagles. Along the way, the Commanders will also need to leapfrog the 5-6 Cowboys. Still, it's far from crazy to think the Commanders can pull it off. However it plays out, the Commanders have added a player who will potentially help them navigate the remaining schedule in a way that vaults them into the postseason. Who knows? Maybe Aiyuk will get a chance to return to Santa Clara in January. And maybe the Commanders will get a chance to do what they nearly did in Week 6. That's still weeks away. But it will be here quickly. And Commanders-49ers is one of the various potential permutations that could play out as the playoffs approach and the postseason commences.

title: Kyren Williams makes it 13-3 Rams in second quarter
summary: The Rams have had the ball three times and all three drives have ended in points.
content: The Rams have had the ball three times and all three drives have ended in points. Running back Kyren Williams finished off the third possession with a seven-yard sprint into the end zone that pushed the Rams' lead over the Packers to 13-3 with 11:29 to play in the first half. It's the first time the Rams have scored on their first three possessions this season and it's also the first time the Packers have allowed their opponents points on their first three drives. Most of the other movement on the drive came through the air. Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford completed passes to Williams, tight end Davis Allen, wide receiver Konata Mumpfield, and tight end Tyler Higbee for first downs before Williams's touchdown. The throw to Williams came just before Stafford took a hit from Packers defensive end Micah Parsons. Stafford is 10-of-12 for 87 yards while Jordan Love is 6-of-10 for 70 yards, including a 32-yarder to Christian Watson that set up Trey Smack's 54-yard field goal.

title: Micah Parsons gets first sack of season, Packers and Rams tied 13-13 at halftime
summary: Parsons's sack came just before end of the first half in Los Angeles.
content: Packers defensive end Micah Parsons notched his first sack in nearly a year just before halftime in Los Angeles on Wednesday night. Parsons made his return from a torn ACL against the Rams and had a couple of pressures early in the game. He got home for a sack of Matthew Stafford on the Rams' first play after a Trey Smack field goal tied the score at 13-13 with 1:50 to play in the half. The Rams ran out the clock from there and they will get the ball to start the second half at SoFi Stadium. Parsons's sack was part of an eventful final couple of minutes. Rams safety Kamren Kinchens was ejected for a hit to the head of Packers wide receiver Christian Watson and Watson is now being evaluated for a concussion. It would be a big loss for the Packers as Watson has four catches for 65 yards and a touchdown so far on Wednesday night. Running back Kyren Williams scored the Rams' only touchdown, but their offense slowed down after picking up points on each of their first three possessions. Stafford is 12-of-15 for 98 yards while Williams and Blake Corum have 35 yards on nine carries. Packers quarterback Jordan Love is 12-of-18 for 154 yards. The Packers will be hoping for right guard Kevin Zeitler's return from an ankle injury while waiting for more word on Watson and the Rams called tight end Davis Allen to return from an ankle injury.

title: Micah Parsons: Our play in second half Wednesday night was inexcusable
summary: The Rams ran for 195 yards after halftime in their 26-13 win.
content: Packers defensive end Micah Parsons made his return to the lineup against the Rams on Wednesday night, but he wasn't able to help his team to a win in Los Angeles. Parsons picked up a sack late in the first half that sent the game to the break with the score tied 13-13, but he couldn't make an impact in the second half because the Rams barely threw the ball. After running 12 times for 46 yards in the first half, the Rams ran 35 times for 194 yards while outscoring the Packers 13-0 in the final 30 minutes. After the game, Parsons said it is "just inexcusable" to allow opposing teams to "dictate games like that" and said the aftermath has to be an increased level of accountability for the entire defense. "We need to figure out who's going to be a dog or not," Parsons said. "That’s just the reality of it. To me, to be honest and this is around the league, if someone can line up 50 times and run down your mouth and you don't have an answer for it, that is player — that's accountability. That's just how I really feel about it. I wasn't able to get on the field because of it, because they didn't want to waste my plays on first and second down I think the whole thing is just bad and we've got to figure out who's willing to play with us or who's playing against us at this point." The Packers don't have the luxury of having time to figure things out. The loss dropped them to 6-5 on the season and the makeup of the NFC means that they're going to have to win most of their remaining games to have any chance of advancing to the postseason.

title: NFL Playoff Picture 2026: Updated AFC and NFC standings, bracket, tiebreakers for Week 12
summary: The five-game football feast surrounding Thanksgiving has major playoff implications for all 10 teams playing around the holiday, and it started with the Rams moving into playoff position with a win over the Packers.
content: The five-game football feast surrounding Thanksgiving has major playoff implications for all 10 teams playing around the holiday, and it started with the Rams moving into playoff position with a win over the Packers. We look at the playoff race for Week 12 below: AFC Playoff Picture DIVISION LEADERS 1. Bills (9-1): Will have the inside track for the No. 1 seed if they win on Thanksgiving night against the Chiefs. 2. Broncos (8-2) : Currently ahead of the Chiefs in the AFC West based on the better record in common games 3. Jaguars (7-3) : Loss to the Giants was a big blow to their hopes of earning the No. 1 seed in the AFC. 4. Bengals (7-3) : In control of the AFC North, but Monday night's loss in Washington hurts. WILD CARDS 5. Chiefs (8-2): Huge game coming against the Bills on Thanksgiving night. 6. Browns (6-4) : Cleveland's path to the playoffs is looking surprisingly easy. 7. Steelers (6-4) : Major questions about the direction of this team after benching Aaron Rodgers. OUTSIDE LOOKING IN 8. Patriots (5-5) : Hard to see them competing without Drake Maye. 9. Texans (4-6) : Running out of time to go on a run. 10 Raiders (4-7): The rest of the season is about developing Fernando Mendoza. 11. Ravens (4-7) : Lamar Jackson's injury just about killed their playoff hopes. 12. Jets (3-8): Aaron Glenn is on the hot seat. 13. Colts (3-8) : No longer competing. 14. Chargers (1-9) : The NFL's most disappointing team. 15. Dolphins (1-9) : The playoffs this year were never a realistic possibility. 16. Titans (1-9): Need to figure out if Cam Ward is their quarterback. NFC Playoff Picture DIVISION LEADERS 1. 49ers (9-1) : Inside track for the No. 1 seed after a big win Sunday night against the Vikings. 2. Lions (8-2) : First place in the NFC North is on the line in the Thanksgiving showdown with the Bears. 3. Giants (6-3-1) : Clear path to the playoffs in John Harbaugh's first season. 4. Panthers (5-5): Best record in the NFL's worst division. WILD CARDS 5. Bears (8-2) : They'll lead the division if they beat the Lions on Thanksgiving, but if they lose they'll be 0-3 in the NFC North. 6. Vikings (7-3): Have lost three of their last four after a hot start. 7. Rams (7-4) : Big win on Thanksgiving Eve against the Packers moved them back into playoff position. OUTSIDE LOOKING IN 8. Seahawks (6-4) : Sunday's game in San Francisco is a big one. 9. Packers (6-5): The Thanksgiving Eve loss to the Rams dropped them out of playoff position. 10. Cowboys (5-6) : It won't be easy to catch the Giants in the NFC East. 11. Commanders (4-5-1) : May need to run the table to win the division. 12. Buccaneers (3-7) : Still in the race in the terrible NFC South. 13. Falcons (3-7) : Still in the race in the terrible NFC South. 14. Saints (3-7) : Still in the race in the terrible NFC South. 15. Eagles (3-7) : Showed some fight in upsetting the Steelers. 16. Cardinals (3-8) : Worst team in the NFC.

title: On Our Way Home is free on Thursday and Friday
summary: The holiday season is here.
content: The holiday season is here. And I'm in the mood to give something away. (It must be the whiskey.) The On Our Way Home ebook is available for free on Thursday and Friday. Why not give something away? This is the week when everyone is trying to sell you something. No one is giving you anything, with zero strings attached. On Our Way Home is primarily a Christmas story. It's also a ghost story. I cranked it out between Thanksgiving and New Year's Day a few years back. In the interests of avoiding any spoilers, I'll just say this: Download it and give it a try. It's essentially about family and redemption and reconciliation. It's also about forgiving others, while finding a way to forgive yourself. It's funny at times. It's sad at times. If you make it to the end, you'll possibly shed a tear or two. The best feedback I've gotten came from a reader who had suffered from PTSD for years. Reading On Our Way Home unlocked his ability to feel emotions again. I never intended anything like that. I just had an idea for a story, years before writing it. One year, I got caught up in the spirit of the season and it flowed, one chapter, one page, one word at a time. The price is right. If you don't like it, delete it. If you like it, keep going. Speaking of free, Quarterback of the Future is being posted , one chapter at a time. Twenty-five chapters are up. A new one is coming every day until it's done. Someone asked recently why my break from writing consists of more writing. There's something magical and, frankly, fun about creating something out of nothing. It's even more fun when people read it and enjoy it. Whether you enjoy it is up to you. If you don't, that's on me. But it won't cost you a penny to find out, if you download On Our Way Home on Thursday or Friday.

title: Rams extend lead to 6-0 after Tucker Kraft fumble
summary: The Rams doubled their lead after forcing the first turnover of Wednesday night's game.
content: The Rams doubled their lead after forcing the first turnover of Wednesday night's game. Linebacker Nate Landman punched the ball out of tight end Tucker Kraft's hands and safety Quentin Lake recovered the ball on the Rams' 43-yard-line. The play came one snap after a Kam Curl interception was wiped out by an illegal contact penalty. The Rams picked up a first down when Packers defensive tackle Devonte Wyatt was flagged for roughing Matthew Stafford and added another on a 15-yard pass to Konata Mumpfield. Packers defensive end Micah Parsons pressured Stafford into an incompletion on the next play and a botched backward pass cost the Rams six yards before they settled for Brandon McManus's second field goal. It's now 6-0 with 3:12 to play in the first quarter.

title: Rams lead 3-0, Christian Watson makes quick return from thigh injury
summary: The Rams are out to an early lead at SoFi Stadium.
content: The Rams are out to an early lead at SoFi Stadium. After forcing a quick Packers punt, the Rams ran three times for a first down. Matthew Stafford's first pass of the game was a deep shot to wide receiver Xavier Smith that fell incomplete, but Packers rookie cornerback Brandon Cisse was flagged for pass interference. The play picked up 37 yards for the home team, but three straight completions by Stafford only picked up seven more yards and Brandon McManus was called on for a field goal that made it 3-0 with 9:55 to play in the first quarter. The Packers opened the game with a six-yard pass to wide receiver Christian Watson, but he needed medical attention after the play. The team called him questionable to return with a thigh injury, but he was back on the field after the Rams kicked the ball off.

title: Rams move ahead 20-13 on Blake Corum TD
summary: The Rams took more than eight minutes off the clock before taking the lead.
content: The Rams let Blake Corum do most of the heavy lifting on their opening drive of the second half. Corum ran nine time for 35 yards during a 15-play Rams drive and the final yard he picked up was a touchdown that broke a tie and put the Rams up 13-10. The drive opened the third quarter and ate up eight minutes of playing time. The Rams faced three third downs on the drive and had Matthew Stafford throw to wide receiver Konata Mumpfield each time. The first two were completions that picked up 30 yards and the third was initially ruled a touchdown on the field. Replays showed Mumpfield did not have control of the ball in the end zone, but the Rams still got a first down due to a defensive holding penalty on the day. Corum has 16 carries for 58 yards and Mumpfield has four catches for 69 yards.

title: Rams S Kamren Kinchens ejected for hit on Christian Watson
summary: Rams safety Kamren Kinchens was ejected from Wednesday night's game against the Packers after a hit on wide receiver Christian Watson.
content: Rams safety Kamren Kinchens was ejected from Wednesday night's game against the Packers after a hit on wide receiver Christian Watson. Per the Netflix broadcast, the league office said that Kinchens was ejected for leaving his feet and making helmet-to-helmet contact with Watson and NFL executive vice president Troy Vincent made the final call on disqualifying him from the game. Watson held onto the ball, but went to the locker room with members of the medical staff and the catch did not count because Packers wideout Matthew Golden was flagged for offensive pass interference to offset the Kinchens foul. The play came on a fourth-and-1 and the Packers ultimately opted to kick a field goal rather than go for it again. It is now 13-13 with under two minutes to play in the half.

title: Rams shut down Packers in second half for a 26-13 win in NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve game
summary: The Rams running game powered them to their fifth straight win.
content: The Rams and Packers played to a tie in the first 30 minutes of Wednesday night's game in Los Angeles, but the second half was all Rams. Blake Corum ran for 151 yards and a score in final 30 minutes and the Rams defense shut out the Packers to pave the way to a 26-13 win. The victory is the fifth in a row for the Rams and they are now 7-4 with a Thursday night home game against the Chiefs on deck in Week 13. The win moves the Rams ahead of the Packers in the race for NFC playoff spots and Thursday's game between the Lions and Bears will have further impact on the chances for all four teams to advance to the postseason. Corum's touchdown came at the end of the Rams' first possession of the second half and he finished the game with a career-high 32 carries for 184 yards. That scoring drive ate up more than eight minutes. The Packers had a quick three-and-out, but briefly showed some life when linebacker Ty'Ron Hopper picked off Matthew Stafford to set the offense up in Los Angeles territory. Jordan Love turned the ball right back over when he hung a deep pass that safety Jaylen McCullough snagged out of the air. The Rams would then ride Corum and Kyren Williams on a pair of drives that covered more than 11 minutes. The Packers' last chance came with 6:13 left and they moved the ball to midfield before Love threw his second interception of the game. Cornerback Emmanuel Forbes got that one and the Packers were out of timeouts well before the two-minute warning. Sticking with the ground game helped to limit Packers defensive end Micah Parsons's impact in his return from last season's torn ACL. He had a sack late in the first half, but Stafford only threw eight times after the break and the Packers' run defense could not get their offense the ball often enough to get back into the game. Love was 17-of-29 for 198 yards and a touchdown, but clearly missed wide receiver Christian Watson after he left the game with a concussion. They only picked up two first downs after halftime and they'll hope that an extended break before their Week 13 trip to New Orleans is enough time for him to return to action. The Rams have several injuries of their own to monitor as guard Bill Murray joined tight ends Davis Allen and Tyler Higbee in making early exits from the game. They'd like to have all those players back next week, but they showed on Wednesday night that Corum can sometimes be enough all by himself.

title: Report: G.M. Omar Khan called Aaron Rodgers directly to inform him of the benching
summary: As expected, the Steelers view the events that resulted in the benching and eventual release of quarterback Aaron Rodgers differently than Rodgers does.
content: As expected, the Steelers view the events that resulted in the benching and eventual release of quarterback Aaron Rodgers differently than Rodgers does. On one very specific point — as it relates to whether the Steelers properly handled the situation — the Steelers and Rodgers sharply disagree. Rodgers said Wednesday that he learned he'd be benched and inactive when tight end Pat Freiermuth called Rodgers, after the announcement of the move was made at 11:10 p.m. ET on Tuesday night. However, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reported during the Wednesday night pregame show that G.M. Omar Khan called Rodgers to inform him of the change to Mason Rudolph. It's odd, to say the least, that the Steelers announced the move after 11:00 p.m. local time on a Tuesday night. If Rodgers didn't know, there was no reason to let the world (and specifically the Broncos) know the move had been made. The mere fact that the Steelers announced it when they did suggests that Rodgers knew about the decision, and that the Steelers believed he possibly would release it in terms that supported his broader version of the events. By announcing it on Tuesday night, the Steelers pre-empted a late-night social-media post from Rodgers — or a strategic leak to a reporter — painting the situation in the light most favorable to Rodgers. For example, Rodgers could have characterized that he was benched because he was repeatedly blowing the whistle internally about coach Mike McCarthy's various alleged lapses. While it's a minor point, it points to the broader issue of credibility. If Rodgers knew about the decision, any suggestion that he didn't would be calculated to make the Steelers look inept for telling the world he'd been benched without letting him know about it in advance. The truth may never be fully known. But it's clear that, as to the things that happened over the past day or two, there are (as there always seems to be) two versions — Rodgers's version and the team's version. It's also possible there are three versions. Rodgers's version, the Steelers' version, and the truth.

title: Romeo Doubs, Alijah Vera-Tucker return to Patriots practice
summary: A.J.
content: A.J. Brown remains out of Patriots practice, but they got another wide receiver back on the field on Wednesday. Romeo Doubs took part in practice as a limited participant. He has been out with a shoulder injury since Week 6 of the regular season. The Patriots also got guard Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) back on the field. Both players are now in 21-day windows to be activated from injured reserve. Brown is sidelined by a hamstring injury. Quarterback Drake Maye (ankle), cornerback Carlton Davis (knee), and offensive lineman Walter Rouse (concussion protocol) were the other Patriots out of practice ahead of Sunday's game against the Chargers. Fullback Reggie Gilliam (knee) was also limited and guard Ben Brown (knee) was a full participant.

title: Steelers should have known Aaron Rodgers, Mike McCarthy couldn't co-exist
summary: Someone in the organization should have said a reunion cannot happen.
content: When the Steelers hired coach Mike McCarthy, we cautioned against assuming that this meant there would be a reunion between McCarthy and quarterback Aaron Rodgers. That position assumed there would be a commonsense assessment of the specific history of McCarthy and Rodgers in Green Bay by those with the power to bring them together for the present and the future. The reporting of Tyler Dunne, who at the time wrote for Bleacher Report , made it clear that there were issues between them during the latter years of McCarthy's time with the Packers. Rodgers took it to another level on Wednesday, telling Pat McAfee and company that McCarthy believed Rodgers got him fired by the Packers — and that McCarthy had done some of the things he's been doing with the Steelers when McCarthy coached the Packers. If McCarthy believes Rodgers got him fired by the Packers, why in the world would McCarthy want Rodgers in his Pittsburgh locker room? It's ludicrous. It's asinine. It's self-destructive. From Rodgers's perspective, why in the world would he want to play for McCarthy again? Although Rodgers said Wednesday that he believed McCarthy would be different given it's Rodgers's last year in the NFL and McCarthy's first year in his dream job, it was naive for Rodgers to think that, at 63, McCarthy would suddenly start working harder than he ever has. Oh, they tried to sell us on the idea that he would. " Attention to detail " became a talking point during training camp. Plenty of media members swallowed the hook. Rodgers knew better. But he ignored his own experiences with McCarthy — in the same way McCarthy ignored his own experiences with Rodgers. The situation cried out for someone, anyone in the organization to stand up and say, "Are we nuts? Once adversity strikes, this situation will crumble. And it will take us with it." It didn't just crumble. It imploded into one of the most embarrassing situations any NFL franchise has endured in years, if not ever. As the saying goes, when you dance with the devil, you don't change the devil. The devil changes you. By allowing McCarthy and Rodgers to reprise their Lambeau rumba, the Steelers thought the music would stop in the postseason. Instead, McCarthy and Rodgers have pulled a franchise with six Super Bowl trophies into the eighth circle of dysfunction. In the end, the team in the city known for blast furnaces has found itself in football hell.

title: T.J. Lang blasts "despicable" Aaron Rodgers comments about Mike McCarthy
summary: T.J.
content: T.J. Lang blocked for Aaron Rodgers for eight seasons in Green Bay. Currently, Lang would be more inclined to knock Rodgers on his ass. Lang sharply criticized Rodgers for his decision to go public with issues that should have stayed in the Pittsburgh locker room. “ I think it’s despicable ,” Lang said on 97.1 The Ticket in Detroit, via Sean Keeley of Awful Announcing . “I think that Aaron Rodgers just became everything that he has bitched about and moaned about over the last 10 years with former coaches, former teammates, airing grievances out, giving opinions out in the media. “He has blacklisted, I don’t know how many, former teammates from just simple comments telling the truth because he just — he was sick of it. Honestly, I don’t even know if I want to watch the whole thing. It’s just unnecessary. It’s a victim mentality. It’s a 'poor me, woe is me. Oh, I thought this, and it wasn’t that.’ And I’m sick, man. “I’ve been in a group chat with a whole lot of former teammates that feel the exact same way that I do.” Most football players would feel that way. There's a code in the locker room. Rodgers violated it. “Mike McCarthy was my head coach for 8 years, and I love Mike McCarthy,” Lang said. “And I talked to Mike McCarthy on Monday night, and still have a great relationship with him. “I haven’t talked to Aaron Rodgers in probably 5 years. I can’t remember the last time he returned a text. I don’t have a relationship with him. And I think it’s just absolutely despicable what he just did to Big Mike.” Rodgers isn't a whistleblower. He's a troublemaker. He didn't get his way, so he emptied a can of gasoline and tossed a match over his shoulder on the way out the door. How does any of it help his now-former teammates? Rodgers's decision to air out dirty laundry has created a massive distraction that will do nothing to help the team win. Accurate or not, the task at hand becomes harder now that everyone is buzzing about Rodgers's comments. That said, no one should be surprised. It's part and parcel of doing business with Rodgers. When it ends — and end it will — it will end poorly. Like it did in Green Bay. Like it did in New York. Like it did in Pittsburgh. Like it will end for his next team, if there is one. And if there is, the message is clear. Buyer beware.

title: The clock is ticking on Mike McCarthy's time with the Steelers
summary: McCarthy's future likely hinges on his ability to win games down the stretch.
content: When it comes to the nuclear war of words that Aaron Rodgers started on Wednesday, the end result is the same as it would be if the world's superpowers ever started hunting and pecking the launch codes. Mutually assured destruction. Rodgers, as multiple former Green Bay Packers are making clear, is destroying his reputation and legacy as a teammate by breaking the fundamental code of the locker room. But he's also destroying Mike McCarthy's reputation and legacy as a coach. For a change, Rodgers's rant was centered in reality. ESPNFL reports that the things Rodgers said about McCarthy are true . Which could make it impossible for the Steelers to keep McCarthy beyond the 2026 season. His only path to salvation is to win. Starting on Friday, when the 8-2 Broncos come to town for a game against a Steelers team that, despite the sudden dysfunction, is 6-4. It's really that simple. The next seven games will become the litmus test as to whether McCarthy's now-documented snoring-and-ice-cream-sandwiches flaws are outweighed by his capabilities. Of course, the fact that Rodgers rolled a grenade into the locker room on his way out won't make that any easier. Which could be one of the reasons why Rodgers did it. Maximum chaos will make it harder for McCarthy to win. Which will make it harder for McCarthy to make it to Year 2. Which will create the impression that Rodgers has been vindicated. Sure, the initial word is that the situation doesn't impact McCarthy's standing. But the most important aspect of Wednesday's report from ESPNFL that McCarthy " has the full support of the organization " carries an important qualifier. The Steelers are "not planning to make any immediate changes." So they're not firing McCarthy or asking him to resign before Friday's game. What happens if the Steelers lose by double digits to the Broncos? What happens if the current two-game losing streak becomes an extended skid that sweeps them out of the AFC postseason field? The answer will become obvious based on how the final seven games unfold. In the immediate aftermath of Aaron Rodgers dumping Agent Orange on the organization, it's hard to imagine McCarthy surviving this. Ultimately, the decision will be made by owner Art Rooney II. And the outcome could show where the Steelers reside on the line that divides the functional from dysfunctional franchises. Functional teams admit mistakes and commence rectifying them. Dysfunctional teams deny the facts and double down.

title: The Lions, despite their resurgence, are 1-8 in their last nine Thanksgiving games
summary: The Lions commenced their ongoing resurgence in 2022.
content: The Lions commenced their ongoing resurgence in 2022. That hasn't translated to sustained success on Thanksgiving. They're 1-8 over the last nine Thanksgiving Day games. The one win in that stretch came two years ago, against the Bears. That day, Chicago pocketed a timeout as the final 30 seconds or so ticked away, leaving the Bears without enough time to attempt a field goal that would have forced overtime in a 23-20 game. The next day, the Bears fired coach Matt Eberflus. It paved the way for the eventual hiring of Lions offensive coordinator Ben Johnson, who returns to Ford Field today for the second time. Last year's game didn't go very well. Detroit scored 52 points. The Bears lost the Soldier Field rematch, too. This year, history takes a back seat to the immediate future. Both the Bears and the Lions are 8-2. The Lions have won all six of their home games. The winner takes control, for now, of the NFC North — and stays within striking distance of the 9-1 49ers for the No. 1 seed. It's not hyperbole to call it the most significant early-window Thanksgiving game ever. In many years, the Lions were the punching bag on turkey day. They're now the ones doing the punching. Which makes the 1-8 trend even more surprising. For the Bears, the challenge is to prove that they're Super Bowl contenders. They entered the discussion with their Week 8 Monday night win in Seattle. Today, the Bears have a chance to control the narrative. However it goes, the numbers should be eye-popping. For last year's Packers-Lions game, 47.7 million tuned in. It was a new all-time regular-season record audience, until Chiefs-Cowboys later that day shattered it with 57.23 million viewers. All three games could be compelling today. Eagles-Cowboys got a boost from both teams winning on Sunday. And Chiefs-Bills continues to be one of the top rivalries in the league — even if cold and wind and rain could take more than a little steam out of the offenses. Enjoy the day. We'll be here throughout the games, posting all relevant updates and other NFL news. It's a privilege, not a burden, to spend time on Thanksgiving doing what we always do. And we're thankful for the fact that you choose to consume it.

title: Tony Romo re-emerges, as an employee of a gambling company
summary: The unofficial path for a sports-media second act is becoming more and more clear.
content: The unofficial path for a sports-media second act is becoming more and more clear. Go gambling, young man . Tony Romo, whose career with CBS ended earlier this year in the aftermath of a DUI arrest that would have been overlooked if the company was otherwise happy with his work, will be the " chief predictions officer " at Betr. The press release leans in to Romo's reputation for being able to predict plays before they happen. This overlooks the fact that he got away from doing that after his first year or so in the CBS booth. It also glosses over the reality that his access to practice and production meetings equipped him with the ability to make "predictions" that (based on his inside information) also could be called "spoilers." It's not entirely clear what he'll be doing. The release says that Romo will "serve as a prominent face of the Betr brand, appearing in original content, delivering sports predictions and engaging fans across the company's expanding ecosystem of gaming products." Of course, Betr won't want his predictions to be too accurate — as it relates to its sportsbook. The sportsbooks only win when the customers lose. If the customers win too much, the sportsbook will land in one of two chapters: 11 or 7. Prediction markets are different. The companies make money on the transactions, with the participants balancing out wins and losses in the zero-sum game of who's right and who's wrong. The next question is whether this is the first step for Romo, or whether it's his primary post-CBS play. With the NFL and its broadcast partners aligned with the Coke and Pepsi of sports gambling, Romo's relationship with one of the various companies that hopes to establish itself as the RC Cola won't improve his shot at getting back into a prominent position in a broadcast booth. Regardless, Romo is back. At least he's not working for an illegal offshore sportsbook. Either way, his message will be the same to the masses as it is to those who are looking for a fresh foothold in sports media. Go gambling, young man.
